faq.q: Which symbols are allowed in Roblox display names?
faq.a: Single-character Unicode symbols such as ★ ♡ ✦ ❀ ⋆ ✧ are the most reliable: they pass Roblox's name filter and render in-game. Obscure Unicode blocks and long multi-character combos are more likely to be rejected. Every symbol in the Roblox-Friendly section above is chosen because it reliably saves.

faq.q: Why does Roblox block some symbols?
faq.a: Roblox runs an automatic content/name filter to keep names readable and safe. It rejects characters it can't validate: many decorative or rare Unicode characters, invisible characters, and some combos. If a symbol won't save in your display name, swap it for a simpler single-character alternative.

faq.q: How do I add symbols to my Roblox display name?
faq.a: Click a symbol on this page to copy it, then paste it into Settings → Account Info → Display Name (or your group/bio field). Display name accepts symbols; the underlying @username does not: that field is letters, numbers, and one underscore only.

faq.q: Are these Roblox symbols safe to use?
faq.a: Yes. They are ordinary Unicode characters used for decoration, not exploits or workarounds, so using them in a display name or bio doesn't violate Roblox's rules. Just keep your overall name appropriate: the content filter still applies to the words around the symbols.

faq.q: Can you copy and paste the real Robux, Premium, or Verified icon?
faq.a: No. Those icons are private-use Unicode codepoints (U+E000–U+E003) mapped to glyphs in Roblox's own client icon font, documented on the official Roblox Developer Forum. They only render inside a game's UI that a developer builds in Roblox Studio: not in a display name, bio, chat, or anywhere off-platform. Pasted elsewhere they show up blank. The crown, checkmark, and diamond symbols in the Status & Rank section above are the closest paste-safe look, without claiming to be an official badge.

faq.q: Why did a symbol work for someone else but show "unsupported characters" for me?
faq.a: Roblox's name filter isn't perfectly consistent: behavior can vary by account region, app version, or which characters surround the symbol. If a combo fails, try pasting just the single symbol on its own first, then rebuild the combo one character at a time. Single-character picks from the Roblox-Friendly Symbols section are the most reliable starting point.

faq.q: What characters does Roblox actually support in display names?
faq.a: Roblox's display name field supports a wide range of Unicode (letters, numbers, and many symbols) but it's filtered, not fully open. There's no official published allow-list, so "supported" in practice means "passes the current filter," which can shift over time. The safest bet is the single-character picks in the Roblox-Friendly Symbols section above; multi-character combos and rarer Unicode blocks are more likely to be rejected.

faq.q: Do Japanese, Chinese, or Korean characters work in a Roblox display name?
faq.a: It varies by account. Some players on the official Developer Forum report full CJK names like こんにちは or 안녕하세요 passing, but 2026 reports show Japanese display names rejected with an 'Unsupported characters' error. Latin letters with diacritics (é, ü, ł, and similar accented characters) get rejected too. Test the name in the display-name box before you commit to it.

faq.q: How do I put a space in my Roblox display name?
faq.a: Roblox trims real spaces at the start and end of a display name and rejects a field left empty after trimming, so a literal space alone won't save. Use an invisible character instead: Hangul Filler (ㅤ) or Braille Pattern Blank (⠀) from the Invisible & Blank Roblox Names section aren't classified as whitespace, so they hold a visual gap without getting stripped.
